also.hook: Hinton kept faith with neural networks through two AI winters, and won. The training method he championed in 1986 and the 2012 breakthrough his lab produced turned a marginal idea into the technology behind modern AI. Then, at the peak of vindication, he quit Google to warn the world about what he had helped build, giving AI risk its most credentialed voice.
also.name: Geoffrey Hinton

name: Pioneers and Historical Figures
blurb: The people whose work the field is built on, including those who died before it had a name.

profiles.hook: A century before electronic computers existed, Lovelace saw what they would become. Her 1843 notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine contain the first published algorithm written for a machine, and, more radically, the first argument that such machines could work on any symbol, not just numbers. Every general-purpose computer vindicates that insight.
profiles.name: Ada Lovelace

quote.text: The Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything. It can do whatever we know how to order it to perform.
quote.context: Note G, from her notes on the Analytical Engine, 1843

primary.name: Sketch of the Analytical Engine, with notes by the translator (full text of Notes A-G)

timeline.impact: Begins the collaboration that defines her work

timeline.event: Resumes advanced study under Augustus De Morgan
timeline.impact: Builds the mathematical footing for the notes

timeline.impact: First published algorithm; theory of general-purpose computation
Work lies dormant until the computing age rediscovers it

quick_facts: Wrote the first published algorithm intended for a machine, the notes to Babbage's Analytical Engine (1843)
First to argue a computing machine could manipulate symbols beyond numbers, music included
Daughter of the poet Lord Byron; tutored by mathematician Augustus De Morgan
The Ada programming language (U.S. DoD, 1980) is named for her

achievements.title: Notes on the Analytical Engine (1843)
achievements.impact: Her translation of Menabrea's paper tripled in length with her own notes A through G, turning an engineering description into a theory of general computation.

achievements.title: Note G: the first published machine algorithm
achievements.impact: A step-by-step method for computing Bernoulli numbers on the Engine, recognized as the first published program.

achievements.title: The 'poetical science' thesis
achievements.impact: Her claim that the Engine could act on symbols under rules, weaving 'algebraical patterns' the way the Jacquard loom weaves flowers, prefigured symbolic computation and, by extension, AI.

achievements.title: The Lovelace objection
achievements.impact: Her caution that the Engine 'can do whatever we know how to order it to perform' framed the machine-originality debate Turing answered directly in 1950, and that AI researchers still argue.

profiles.hook: Turing supplied both of AI's founding documents: the 1936 paper proving one universal machine could compute anything computable, and the 1950 paper asking whether machines can think. The first made computers possible; the second made artificial intelligence a research question rather than a fantasy.
profiles.name: Alan Turing

quote.text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
quote.context: Closing line of Computing Machinery and Intelligence, Mind, 1950

profiles.moniker: Father of Theoretical Computer Science and AI

timeline.event: Joins Bletchley Park the day after Britain declares war
Publishes Computing Machinery and Intelligence in Mind
Convicted of 'gross indecency' for his homosexuality
timeline.impact: Career destroyed by the state he had served

timeline.event: Receives royal pardon; 'Turing's Law' follows in 2017

quick_facts: Defined the universal computing machine (1936), the mathematical model every computer still follows
Led the Hut 8 team at Bletchley Park breaking German naval Enigma in WWII
Proposed the imitation game, now the Turing Test, in 1950
The Turing Award, computing's highest honor, bears his name

achievements.title: On Computable Numbers (1936)
achievements.impact: Introduced the Turing machine and universal computation, the theoretical basis of every computer built since.

achievements.title: Breaking naval Enigma at Bletchley Park (1939-1945)
achievements.impact: The bombe machines and Banburismus methods he devised shortened the Atlantic war; historians credit the effort with saving vast numbers of lives.

achievements.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
achievements.impact: Reframed 'can machines think?' as an operational test, predicted machine learning, and answered Lovelace's objection, the founding paper of AI.

achievements.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
achievements.impact: Founded mathematical biology with reaction-diffusion theory, showing his computational lens reached beyond machines.
